title: Why shoots lean toward light
question: How does a shoot sense where the light is and bend toward it?
hook: Put a plant by a window and its stem slowly curves toward the glass.
idea: Auxin gathers on the shaded side of a shoot, so cells there grow longer and tip the plant toward the light.

beats.prompt: Light shines on a shoot only from the right. Where does auxin move, and what happens?

choices.label: To the shaded left side, whose cells lengthen so the shoot curves right
To the lit right side, whose cells lengthen so the shoot curves left
choices.feedback: It tempts because light seems to drive growth, but auxin moves to the shaded side.

choices.label: It stays spread evenly, so the shoot grows straight up
choices.feedback: Light from one side is exactly what shifts auxin; an even spread would give no bending.

beats.explain: In asymmetric light, auxin moves to the shaded side and promotes elongation of the cells there, curving the plant toward the light.

beats.prompt: put these steps in the order they happen in a bending shoot
items: Asymmetric light shifts auxin to the shaded side
Auxin activates proton pumps, lowering the pH in those cells
Acid activates expansins, which loosen the cell walls
The cells swell, driving the shoot's bend
beats.explain: Auxin moves first, then the proton pumps acidify the wall, expansins loosen it, and the swelling cells push the shoot to bend.

beats.prompt: match each phototropism player to its role
pairs: Promotes cell elongation on the shaded side
Main auxin carrier, setting where auxin collects
The very tip, needed for light sensing
beats.explain: Each one handles a different step, from sensing light to moving auxin to loosening walls.

beats.prompt: one step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A shoot gets light only from one side.
Auxin moves toward the shaded side.
Auxin there makes the cells shorter, which tilts the shoot toward the light.
So the plant curves toward the light source.
beats.explain: Auxin promotes elongation of the cells on the shaded side; longer cells on that side are what curve the shoot toward the light.
